label: Susan Leigh Star
line: Sociologist of infrastructure, classification and invisible work.

label: Paul Dourish
line: Computer scientist who studies the materialities of information.

label: Nafis Hasan
line: Writes on India's digital governance and data repair.

label: Lev Manovich
line: Media theorist of the database and new media.

label: Graham M. Jones
line: Anthropologist; writes here on how sorting shapes thinking.

label: Martin Heidegger
line: The syllabus starts from his inheritance: technology as an abstraction, an index of modernity, the world captured as a resource.

label: Erwin Panofsky
line: Art historian who called linear perspective a symbolic form; Manovich builds on him (spelled "Ervin" in the article).

label: Langdon Winner
line: Political theorist of technology: Autonomous Technology (1977), "Do Artifacts Have Politics?" (1986, as Star cites it).

label: Charles Perrow
line: Sociologist of organizations and accidents.

label: Anson Rabinbach
line: Historian of labor, fatigue and the human motor.

label: Geoffrey Bowker
line: Star's collaborator; Star credits him with infrastructural inversion, and Dourish cites him too.

label: Rob Nixon
line: Slow Violence and the Environmentalism of the Poor (2011); Hasan cites him.

label: Niklas Luhmann
line: Sociologist whose slip box (Zettelkasten) Jones discusses.

label: Yuk Hui
line: Philosopher of technology: cosmotechnics, digital objects.

label: Infrastructure is relational
line: Not a thing but a relation: one person's background is another person's job, or obstacle.

label: Visible upon breakdown
line: Working infrastructure is invisible; it appears when it breaks.

label: Study boring things
line: Lists of numbers, technical specifications, hidden mechanisms: Star's call to look at them.

label: Built on an installed base
line: New infrastructure has to wrestle with the inertia of what is already there.

label: Embodiment of standards
line: Infrastructure carries standards and plugs into other tools and conventions.

label: Learned as part of membership
line: Newcomers learn the infrastructure; for insiders it is taken for granted.

label: Infrastructural inversion
line: Bring the background forward: study what usually sits behind.

label: Ready-to-hand
line: Heidegger's term for a tool in use, which you don't notice; Star uses it without naming him.

label: The world captured as a resource
line: The syllabus's summary of the Heideggerian approach to technology.

label: Symbolic form
line: A culture's way of seeing, built into a form: Panofsky's perspective, Manovich's database.

label: Database vs. narrative
line: A list that refuses to order its items, against a chain of cause and effect: natural "enemies."

label: Games are ruled by the algorithm
line: Manovich: computer games do not follow a database logic but the logic of the algorithm.

label: Paradigm and syntagm
line: New media makes the menu of choices (paradigm) real and the sequence (syntagm) virtual.

label: Materialities of the database
line: Schemas, data models and hardware shape what databasing can be done and imagined.

label: The world as opportunities for databasing
line: Once the database encodes the world, the world starts to look like things to put in a database.

label: The schema
line: A database is open-ended, but only in the terms laid down in its structure.

label: Slow violence
line: Harm that is not spectacular or episodic but slow and concealed, like repair creeping into a life.

label: Vacant citizenship
line: While a record is repaired, the citizen's claims on the state are on hold.

label: Data repair
line: A digital error cannot be corrected digitally: it becomes a legal problem the citizen must fix.

label: Data excess
line: Hasan's term for what database-driven digitization produced.

label: Categorize, recategorize
line: Analysis begins and ends with categories; sorting again makes new ideas.

label: Categorize the categorizing
line: The people you study sort things too: study how they sort.

label: The slip box (Zettelkasten)
line: A filing system of linked cards, after Luhmann: a database you think with.

label: Artifacts have politics
line: Values can be built into technical systems: Winner's question, as Star takes it up.

label: Autonomous technology
line: Technics out of control as a theme in political thought: the subtitle of Winner's book.

label: Complexity and coupling
line: The two terms in Perrow's chapter title. Write in what they mean from your Nov 16 notes.

label: The human motor
line: The body imagined as a machine for work; Rabinbach traces its transformation.

label: Knowledge extractivism
line: AI as an instrument for extracting knowledge, in Pasquinelli and Joler's subtitle.

label: Cosmotechnics
line: Hui's term, in his title: technology joined to a cosmology, so there is more than one.

label: Race as technology
line: Coleman's title, one of the course's opening questions: what if race is seen as a technology?

label: Anticipatory shipping
line: Shipping a package before it is ordered: logistics ahead of time.

label: Infrastructures work on time
line: Mitchell's title: infrastructure as something that works through time.

label: Uptime and downtime
line: Servers kept running, and kept cool: time as a technical demand.

label: The ordinal society
line: A society that ranks: Fourcade and Healy's title.

label: Infrastructure space
line: Easterling's subject: infrastructure as space with power of its own.

label: Disposition
line: Easterling's chapter title. Write in what it means from your Nov 9 notes.

label: Operations of platforms
line: Platforms as a global process, in Mezzadra and Neilson's title.

label: Air as media, cities as computers
line: The course description's provocations: what changes when we see the world this way?
